requiredFindings.finding: On macOS the test asserts matches!(receipt.barrier(), Fsync | FullFlush). DirectoryBarrier has exactly two variants and is not non_exhaustive, so the pattern is irrefutable and the assertion cannot fail. Only the Linux arm discriminates, and Linux is not run. On the only lane executed, the test backs 'binds original owner' and nothing of 'reports actual primitive', while the test name claims both and travels into the frozen evidence as a claim.
requiredFindings.required: Assert the value actually expected on the macOS lane (reviewer probe R5 measures FullFlush), or remove the claim from the test name.

requiredFindings.finding: Reviewer probe R4 measures nlink == 2 for a directory held open after rmdir, so the nlink() == 0 guard never fires on macOS for the case it reads as addressing, and a receipt is granted for a directory with no name anywhere. The inline comment predicts this; the public method documentation does not, and it tells the caller it owes name/custody/filesystem checks without naming what exists. RetainedDirectory::is_reachable is already public and selected, records the same macOS behaviour in its own doc, and answered Ok(false) in exactly the case the barrier accepted.
requiredFindings.required: State on the public method that the link-count guard is best-effort and platform-asymmetric, and name is_reachable() as the existing observation a semantic owner must call itself. Disclosure only — do not wire is_reachable into the barrier, which would silently widen the primitive.

requiredFindings.finding: attempted is held while after is sampled and attempted? is applied last, so (a) when the flush fails and the post-sample condition also fails the caller receives InvalidData 'retained directory changed' and the barrier's io::Error is dropped, and (b) when the flush fails and the post metadata() call itself errors the caller receives the metadata error. Both fail closed, but the same doc says semantic owners must stop the act, and an owner that must classify the failure cannot when the underlying error has been replaced without notice.
requiredFindings.required: Document which error wins and why, or surface both.

observations.note: is_for is handle-object identity, not directory identity (R1); an owner holding two handles on one directory gets false. Safe direction, narrower than 'not equality of caller-supplied pathnames' suggests.

receipts are neither exclusive nor one-shot (R2); &self permits any number of indistinguishable live receipts, so a receipt cannot serve as a capability token. The doc correctly places exclusion on the caller.

the receipt has no Debug, so unwrap_err() on the result does not compile (R7). Legitimate cause — RetainedDirectory has no Debug so a derive is impossible — but NewFileReceipt and ExistingFileReceipt both derive it. A manual impl printing only the barrier variant would remove the inconsistency.
the confirm-time kind guard is unreachable through the public API (R6); the fifth test covers defence in depth behind the private seam, not a public failure mode.

the post-check is thinner than it reads: for an owned descriptor dev, ino and is_dir cannot change, so only the nlink arm can differ, and per RF-2 only on Linux. Two fstat calls per barrier that detect nothing on macOS today.

no new test drives confirm_directory_barrier through the fsync fallback arm; fallback coverage is inherited from two pre-existing tests reaching the private helper or a socket descriptor. R5 confirms FullFlush is what runs.
fixtures use std::env::temp_dir(), i.e. the pinned TMPDIR volume, not a prospective installation-root volume.
the receipt is unforgeable outside the crate, but private fields are visible to descendant modules of filesystem, any of which could construct one directly. None does today.

narrowerLimitationCritique.barrierHalfOnly: My owner390 review recorded two unimplemented native capabilities: a directory-publication primitive and a directory-barrier receipt type. 393 supplies the second. The first does not exist — the exclusive no-replace rename (renameatx_np RENAME_EXCL / renameat2 RENAME_NOREPLACE) is wired only through NativeNewPublication for regular files, and no production path creates a directory at all (create_dir appears only in tests). 393 closes one named half of the 390 TCB gap, not the gap.
narrowerLimitationCritique.doesNotTouchOwner390RF2: The undefined base case in the directory-publication durability recursion is a law-level hole. A primitive that flushes one already-open directory cannot supply a base case; nothing here is progress on it.
narrowerLimitationCritique.whatAReceiptLicenses: this exact in-memory handle had the named barrier primitive applied to its inode, and the inode was still a directory with a non-zero link count immediately afterwards on a platform where that is not evidence of attachment. Not: named, reachable, contained by the intended parent, exclusively held, or durable as a namespace entry. The documentation says the same; the risk is a later caller reading 'directory barrier receipt' as 'the directory is durably published', which RF-2 exists to make harder.
narrowerLimitationCritique.readmeFramingCorrect: exposing this platform primitive adopts none of the unselected 390/392 initialization law
